measure: China export licensing for certain graphite items (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 39 of 2023)
relevance: Licensing on high-purity/high-strength/high-density synthetic graphite and natural flake graphite products gives Beijing visibility and leverage over graphite leaving China, an incentive to process in third countries.
source_name: IEA Policies database (summarising MOFCOM/GACC announcement); corroborated by Mayer Brown and Hogan Lovells (JDSupra)
note: Announced 20 Oct 2023, effective 1 Dec 2023. Claim's 'Dec 2023' is the effective date; the announcement date is 20 Oct 2023. No MOFCOM primary page retrieved; secondary sources (IEA, law firms) agree on number, dates and scope.

measure: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Pub. L. 119-21) signed; PFE / material-assistance limits added to 45X, 45Y, 48E
relevance: Creates the tax-credit test that makes the ownership and origin of anode material inside US-made batteries financially material, which is what makes rerouting through third-country plants relevant.
source_name: IRS Notice 2026-15 (cites Pub. L. 119-21, 139 Stat. 72, July 4, 2025); IRS newsroom; EY Tax News
note: Confirmed via IRS primary text. PFE is defined in IRC 7701(a)(51) and material assistance in 7701(a)(52). For 45Y/48E the material-assistance test applies to facilities beginning construction after 31 Dec 2025; for 45X it applies to components sold in tax years beginning after enactment.

measure: China announces export controls on lithium-battery and artificial graphite anode items (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2025)
relevance: Would have extended Chinese licensing from graphite feedstock to anode materials, cells and anode-making equipment and technology, the inputs that third-country anode plants depend on.
source_name: Fred Gao (translation of MOFCOM/GACC No. 58/2025); CIRS Group; Global Times
note: Issued 9 Oct 2025 with a scheduled effective date of 8 Nov 2025, but suspended before that date (see the 2025-11-07 entry). Not a claim in the original list; added as a newer action.

measure: China suspends Announcements No. 55-58, 61, 62 of 2025 until 10 Nov 2026 (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 70 of 2025)
relevance: The October 2025 anode/battery controls are paused under the US-China truce; the 2023 graphite licensing (No. 39) stays in force.
source_name: CIRS Group; Global Times; Pillsbury; chemradar
note: Legal end date of the suspension was 10 Nov 2026. Outcome (checked 11 Nov 2026): it was not left to lapse. MOFCOM and GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2026, dated 9 Nov 2026, continues the suspension of Announcements 55-58 and 61-62 of 2025 from 11 Nov 2026 to 10 Jan 2027. It does not name Announcement No. 70 but covers the same six measures. See the 2026-11-09 entry.

measure: China suspends paragraph 2 of Announcement No. 46 of 2024 until 27 Nov 2026 (MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 of 2025)
relevance: Pauses China's stricter end-user and end-use review of dual-use graphite going to the US. This is a separate clock from Announcement No. 70, and it ends 17 days later.
source_name: MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 of 2025 (primary); CIRS Group
note: Paragraph 1, the ban on dual-use exports to US military users, stays in force. As of 5 Nov 2026 no extension notice had been found. Re-check after 27 Nov 2026.

measure: Commerce final affirmative AD/CVD determinations on active anode material from China (A-570-194, C-570-195)
relevance: Shows Commerce found Chinese anode material dumped and subsidised at very high rates, which raises the incentive to ship via non-Chinese plants.
source_name: ITA (trade.gov) fact sheet; Federal Register 91 FR 7247 (AD, FR Doc. 2026-02998) and 91 FR 7261 (CVD, FR Doc. 2026-02999)
note: CORRECTED: announced 11 Feb 2026 but published in the Federal Register on 17 Feb 2026 (both notices 'applicable February 17, 2026'), not around 11 Feb. AD: 93.50% for the separate-rate exporters/producers (including BTR, Shanshan, Zhongke Shinzoom combinations); China-wide entity 102.72%. CVD: 66.82% (Huzhou Kaijin; AFA) and 66.86% (Panasonic Global Procurement China and All Others), so '~66.8%' should read 66.82-66.86%. The final scope excludes AAM incorporated into lithium-ion battery products (per USITC report).

measure: IRS Notice 2026-15: interim guidance on material assistance from prohibited foreign entities
relevance: Gives the material assistance cost ratio (MACR) method and safe harbors that battery makers use to show their anode inputs are not PFE-sourced. This is where supplier certification of non-Chinese anode origin matters.
note: Confirmed. The notice says little on who counts as a PFE or on effective control; proposed regulations are promised. Comments were due 30 Mar 2026. The statute requires PFE safe-harbor tables by 31 Dec 2026 (per McGuireWoods).

measure: USITC negative final determinations on active anode material from China (701-TA-752, 731-TA-1730)
relevance: Because the Commission voted no, no AD/CVD orders were issued. Chinese anode material pays neither duty today, so the PFE tax-credit test is the live issue. An appeal could reopen the question.
note: CORRECTED wording: the finding was that imports have NOT 'materially retarded the establishment of an industry in the United States', not a standard 'no material injury' finding. Vote was 2-1 (Karpel and Johanson negative; Kearns affirmative). Commerce will not issue AD or CVD orders. The FR notice of the determinations was published 3 Apr 2026 (per the FR document list).

measure: EVE Energy added to the US Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies
relevance: EVE Energy owns the Malaysian cell plant in Case 6. The listing doesn't ban commercial purchases, but it restricts US defense procurement and is a signal buyers screen for.
source_name: Federal Register Doc. 2026-11571 (10 Jun 2026); WilmerHale; Holland & Knight
note: List published 8 Jun 2026; Federal Register notice dated 10 Jun 2026.

measure: MOFCOM says the US–China trade truce runs to 10 Jan 2027
relevance: The political deadline for China's paused graphite and battery export controls moves to Jan 2027, but the legal suspension in Announcement 70 still ends on 10 Nov 2026 unless a new announcement is issued.
source_name: Global Times (MOFCOM statement); China Briefing; Thomson Reuters
note: Checked 5 Nov 2026. No new notice had been found. US and Chinese negotiators are due to meet in Shenzhen later in November.

measure: Status check: further PFE guidance (proposed regs / safe-harbor tables)
relevance: Who counts as a PFE, and the effective-control rules, would determine whether Chinese-owned plants in Indonesia, Morocco or Oman are PFEs.
note: Re-checked 5 Nov 2026: still nothing beyond Notice 2026-15. The safe-harbor tables are due by 31 Dec 2026, and questions on effective control and Hong Kong remain open.

measure: Petitioners ask for a voluntary remand of the USITC's negative anode vote, in an appeal at the Court of International Trade
relevance: If the vote were sent back and reversed, duties on Chinese anode material could return. Single source: a filing by Novonix, a member of the petitioning group. We have not seen the court docket.
source_name: Novonix Form 6-K, 30 Oct 2026 (mirror of SEC filing)
note: Single source. Novonix gives oral argument as the second half of January 2027 and calls a voluntary remand unusual.

measure: UFLPA Entity List updated to 190 entities (91 FR 68159)
relevance: Three genomics companies were added. None of the eight Chinese battery companies checked on this site is listed. Buyers should keep screening, because the list keeps changing.
note: Whole list read on 5 Nov 2026. Checked for BTR, Zhongke, Putailai, EVE, CATL, Gotion, Huayou and Shanshan (the anode maker). The listed 'Hoshine Silicon Industry (Shanshan)' is a different company.

measure: China continues the suspension of its Oct 2025 export controls to 10 Jan 2027 (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2026)
relevance: The October 2025 controls on lithium batteries, artificial graphite anode material and related equipment (Announcement No. 58 of 2025, among others) stay suspended past the 10 Nov 2026 end date of Announcement No. 70. The 2023 graphite licensing (No. 39) is unaffected.
note: Dated 9 Nov 2026; the suspension runs 11 Nov 2026 to 10 Jan 2027. One-sentence text covering Announcements 55, 56, 57, 58 and 61, 62 of 2025. Do not confuse with Announcement No. 58 of 2025 (the battery and graphite controls). Announcement No. 72 of 2025 (end 27 Nov 2026) was not addressed in this text.

measure: BIS extends suspension of the Affiliates Rule through 10 Jan 2027
relevance: The rule extending US export restrictions to foreign firms owned 50% or more by listed parties stays suspended and did not return on 10 Nov 2026.
source_name: Federal Register Doc. 2026-22793 (primary); Dechert; Baker McKenzie
note: Published 9 Nov 2026. Law-firm notes say the rule was released on 5 Nov 2026. The rule is suspended, not withdrawn; it could return after 10 Jan 2027 unless extended again.

measure: BIS Affiliates Rule due to return unless BIS extends its suspension
relevance: Scheduled, not yet an event. The rule would extend US export restrictions to foreign firms owned 50% or more by listed parties. It was the US side of the same deal as Announcement No. 70, whose suspension legally ends the same day.
source_name: Dechert (28 Oct 2026), citing the BIS final rule of 12 Nov 2025
note: Outcome (checked 11 Nov 2026): BIS extended the suspension; the rule did not return on this date. A final rule published 9 Nov 2026 (Federal Register Doc. 2026-22793) extends the suspension through 10 Jan 2027. The rule itself is not repealed or revised. See the 2026-11-09 entry.
